correctness.rationale: Equation (1) in RESULT.md is the Moore--Penrose inverse by three mutually orthogonal eigenspaces of the unnormalized graph Laplacian. Equation (2) gives the four entries (3), with exact sign ordering and multiplicities. Their zero row sums convert the sharp absolute row norm into positive-mass expression (5). The polynomial sign reduction establishes the explicit cutoff and irrationality; branch algebra proves the global bound, both asymptotic limits and extremizing sign masks. The standalone exact-fraction code independently constructs and inverts seven small rank-one shifted Laplacians and tests hundreds of parameter cases. Infinite conclusions rely on the written proof rather than testing. The input norm is on all bounded vertex functions.

originality.rationale: The prior 2003 general Cartesian-product Green formulas are acknowledged as covering the spectral kernel. The mathematically tested new content is the exact rook-graph induced endpoint norm including three sign regimes, a sharp width-squared integer cutoff with optimizer-support change, the global 5/8 sharp bound, and a cubic-rescaled nonanalytic limit profile. Closest primary full texts and published semantic records inspected did not state an equivalent norm-phase theorem. This is bounded, provisional originality, not proof of historical priority.
residual_risks: Ellis gives a generic product Green representation that can be specialized to this matrix. The new element is the absolute-row sharp norm, not the inversion; the claim would lose originality if a pre-existing source explicitly makes the same sign/norm consequence.
Relevant norm results may be indexed under graph signal reconstruction, fundamental matrices or electrical-network stability rather than the queried terminology.
An independent priority assessment, beyond accessible indexed and inspected primary results, has not been undertaken.

value.rationale: For Poisson solutions on grid-like line graphs, exact response amplification under bounded node data is a natural operator invariant. A finite threshold near the square of the short dimension gives permanent norm saturation even though the graph keeps growing, and a sign-mask geometry switch at the same point; this is not a routine single-size calculation. The double scaling recovers a sharply cornered quantitative defect, and the universal maximum identifies the exceptional four-cycle. This infinite-family phase law is a meaningful structural statement with a clear robustness interpretation, independent of any speculative downstream theorem.
